rationale: A last, source-only sharpening of the removed-member refutation rather than a new finding: the same facade loop that carries the removed-node proposal block also filters incoming response messages by membership. Recording that asymmetry makes the contract reading harder to overturn, because it shows the library does consult Progress for one message class and deliberately does not for proposals.

interpretations.rationale: Addendum to the resolution of this question, adding one source observation that strengthens the contract reading. In the same select loop, the receive channel case filters response messages from peers that are not in Progress (the comment reads: filter out response message from unknown From), while the proposal channel case has no membership test, and the removed-node block that nils the proposal channel is the local convenience whose own comment calls the logic unsound and notes that the channel is reset when the leader changes. So within one function the library applies a membership test to responses and declines to apply one to proposals, which is consistent with the documented MsgProp contract that a leader appends what it receives and a follower forwards with the sender's ID, and inconsistent with reading the removed-node block as a guarantee that non-member proposals are rejected. The refutation therefore stands on two independent bases: the documented contract, and the deliberate asymmetry in the facade. No defect is asserted and no execution is claimed; the behaviour facts recorded earlier are unchanged, including that a proposal whose sender is not in the configuration is accepted and appended at the raft level.
limitations: Source-only addendum; no new execution is claimed.

The asymmetry is evidence about intent, not a normative requirement; a reader could still argue the leader ought to check membership, which would be a design change rather than a defect under the current contract.
The upstream comment conceding the channel logic is unsound remains the only statement about the removed-node block, and it is a comment rather than a guarantee.
